description: VUGD, Latvia's State Fire and Rescue Service, publishes statistics on the fires and rescue operations it handles. Its statistics page gives running counts of people killed in fires, 64 in 2025 and 44 so far in 2026, and of people recovered dead from water bodies, with the swimming season shown separately, for each year since 2018. Downloadable reports on rescue work, fires and their consequences cover each year from 2014 to the first half of 2024, and further files cover grass fires from 2014 to 2020, drownings from 2009 to 2018 and fire casualties from 2016 to 2018. Coverage is national. The reports are free and available to download from the VUGD site; no licence terms are stated. Caveats: statistics are published as report tables, not open data, the latest full year report was still for the first half of 2024 when read, and categories change between reports. Simulation uses: calibrating fire and rescue demand, modelling the seasonal peak of grass fires in spring, and comparing Latvian fire death rates with other countries. Related records: the Nordic fire statistics (data-nordic-fire-statistics) include the Baltic states, and the Estonian Rescue Board statistics (data-paasteamet-estonia-rescue-event-statistics) are the neighbouring national source.
